title: Bike the Bay gives cyclists rare chance to ride across Coronado Bridge - NewsBreak
text:
By Rhea Caoile ,
9 hours ago
SAN DIEGO (FOX 5/KUSI) -- The cycling community has something to be excited about coming up later this month -- a scenic ride around the San Diego Bay which includes a chance to travel across the iconic Coronado Bridge.
On Sunday, Aug. 23, people of all ages and abilities are invited to take part in Bike the Bay, an annual fundraiser benefitting the San Diego County Bike Coalition.
Bike the Bay takes cyclists through a 25-mile loop around the Bayshore Bikeway, which begins and ends at the Embarcadero Marina Park South behind the San Diego Convention Center and travels through Coronado, Imperial Beach, Chula Vista and National City.
Cyclists who do not want to do the entire loop around the bay can choose the shorter five-mile route across Coronado Bridge and take the ferry back to the Embarcadero.
Bike the Bay is non-timed and non-competitive, and is instead meant to share people's appreciation for work dedicated to safer and more accessible streets for everyone. Instructions for the event as well as a route map is available on the Bike the Bay website .
Walk-up registration is scheduled to begin at 6 a.m. on the day of the event. The 50-mile ride begins at 6:30 a.m., with the 25-mile ride to follow at 7 a.m. The five-mile ride will begin at 8:30 a.m.
Class I and II e-bikes are allowed at the event with a maximum speed of 20 miles per hour. No other motorized vehicles will be allowed.
Rental bikes are available courtesy of Rad Power Bikes for those who do not have their own bicycles. Troxus is also hosting some promotional rides at the event. Those who are interested in renting on the day of the event are asked to contact organizers online .
A post-ride festival will take place at Embarcadero Marina Park South which will have food, beverages, a beer garden and live entertainment available until 2 p.m. The park is located at 200 Marina Park Way in San Diego.
